survey: Inflatable beach ball on rippled sand, seen from slightly above. The ball is round: the fitted ellipse has a width ratio of 0.97 and is off a true ellipse by 0.7%. It is made of six panels running pole to pole, alternating white, red, white, blue, white and green round the top, which is the standard beach-ball pattern. All six seams meet at a round purple cap on the top pole. The pole is tipped toward the camera, so the cap sits slightly in front of the top edge and the front panels look wider. The red, front white and blue panels narrow toward the bottom pole, which is out of view. The green and back white panels disappear over the back of the ball where expected. The ball touches the sand at its lowest point and casts a contact shadow, so it does not float. No valve is shown, which is an acceptable simplification.
